items.title: John Lamb interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 16, 2001
items.q: I had a trio around Philadelphia and I worked with Jimmy Heath and Specs Wright and Sam Dochre and Kenny Barron.

ctx.x: Well tell me about, in Philadelphia you had some of your own band-leading experiences, didn’t you? Did you lead some of your own groups eventually?

Well I led a group in the Air Force as well. And I had a trio around Philadelphia and I worked with Jimmy Heath and Specs Wright and Sam Dochre and Kenny Barron. Did I tell you I met Kenny Barron? I saw a bass player going into the subway one day. And I says, “hey, where are you going?” He says, “I’m going to a session.” I says, “you mind if I follow you?” So he says, “no, come on.” So I followed him around and he went over this guy’s house, the guy was playing piano. It was Kenny Barron. It was Kenny’s house.…

They had those abilities to do these things. But I discovered that it was more work than just being smart. It was a lot of work. A lot of work. Effort. And a lot of things that I didn’t necessarily want to hear, like I said, musically. I had to go through all of that in order to reach the type of sound that I wanted to reach.
